# Delivery routing ruling (e2e synthetic)

Tanya (team owner) ruled on where reaction delivery belongs:

> we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one
> message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four

Tina pushed back on the batching window and Tanya held: the bundle closes when
the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather
than sending on its own. The alternative considered and rejected was per-skill
delivery with client-side collapsing, which moves the ordering problem onto the
reader.

payload.rationale: The document is a delivery routing ruling by Tanya, so I expanded the three core areas it touches: Narrative_ReactionDeliveryBundling (the narrative frame for reaction notification aggregation), Position_ReactionDeliveryBundlingAndBatchingBoundary (the position on bundling/batching boundaries), and DesignTradeoffs (the area holding the trade-off expressions including the rejected alternative). Actor_Tanya_Staging was expanded to surface both registers — the repeated test-assertion cadence and the decisive owner ruling — so the passes can distinguish this ruling from the background test noise. All five ruling expressions were included at witness depth so the passes have full provenance for the ruling, the pushback-and-hold exchange (relayed through Tina as principal), and the rejected alternative. Narrative_DecisionsEvaporate and Obs_TinaScrollbackQuote were included as broader context: the ruling's concern about cognitive burden ('one thing to read, not four') and Tina's role as pushback voice plausibly connect to the product's foundational narrative about decisions disappearing into scroll-back. I deliberately did NOT expand the style observations (StyleObs_Antithesis_DecisionsEvaporate, StyleObs_ToneDirectPersonal_Quotes) or the Narrative_DefaultRefTopicBranch test-assertion children, as those belong to a different document's rhetorical analysis and a separate test-cadence narrative that this ruling does not bear on.
